title: A telescoping proof of the focal antipedal sum invariant
description:
This preprint proves the focal antipedal distance-sum equality observed by Reznik, Garcia and Koiller as elliptic billiard invariant k603. For every regular closed billiard/Poncelet orbit between strictly nested confocal ellipses, lambda strictly between zero and b squared, the ordinary positive radial-distance sums of the two focal antipedal polygons agree. The proof identifies their per-edge norm difference with a fixed coefficient times the vertical displacement, then uses closure. It covers odd primitive periods, admitted stars, reversal and repeated traversal, without asserting separate constancy of either sum or extending to hyperbolic or degenerate caustics. Standard-library exact rational-chord verification accompanies the self-contained proof.

A bounded primary-source and mechanism audit completed on 6 October 2026 found no earlier full covering result, including a complete comparison of the selected journal final and its precursor. Classical antipedal geometry, the known focal-height product, centrally symmetric cases and telescoping are credited as background. Finite-corpus and source-version limits remain explicit; no absolute-first, exhaustive-literature or continued-open-status guarantee is made. AI tools were used extensively in solving, deriving, drafting, literature checking, code generation, verification and adversarial checking. Independent AI-agent checks are not conventional human peer review. This manuscript is unrefereed and has not received conventional human peer review.
